DuplicateRelationship.description:
Sub-classification used when independence has been rejected.

Distinguishes a likely-duplicate report pair from one where the
pair is linked by something other than being the same individual
case (e.g. same reporter, same study, two patients on the same
unusual regimen). The decision logic chooses between these based
on the weighted inconsistency score ``w_tot``.

Mirrors the user-facing label vocabulary (``Duplicates`` /
``Otherwise_related`` / ``Abstain``).

``ABSTAIN`` is emitted by the shared-source override path for
epistemically underdetermined same-source scenarios: non-independence
is established (same source identifier confirmed) but the available
evidence is insufficient to safely determine whether the reports
describe the same individual. It maps to the user-facing label
``Abstain`` via ``ClassificationResult.final_label``.

See: docs/duplicate_adjudication_spec.md § Independence assessment and § Relationship assessment
DuplicateRelationship.title: DuplicateRelationship

InconsistencyPenalty.description:
The weighted inconsistency score, and the comparison the decision made.

    w_tot = Σ (count × weight)  over the severities present

Self-describing by design: the classifier is the only component that knows
both the inconsistency counts and the configured weights, so it records the
result rather than leaving consumers to recompute it. Recomputing requires
the run's ``DecisionThresholds``, and a consumer that assumes the defaults
will silently disagree with the decision whenever the run used custom
weights.

``threshold`` is the bar this score was tested against, or ``None`` when the
decision made no ``w_tot`` comparison at all — the below-limited zone (where
``L_match`` decides) and ``SAME_SOURCE_DIFFERENT_CASE`` (pinned regardless of
``w_tot``). In those cases the score is still recorded; there is simply no
comparison to report.

See: docs/duplicate_adjudication_spec.md § Relationship assessment
InconsistencyPenalty.title: InconsistencyPenalty

InconsistencySeverity.description:
Severity levels for detected inconsistencies between reports.

See: docs/duplicate_adjudication_spec.md § Severity Levels

Levels:
    minor     – small difference, weakly suggests different individuals
    moderate  – meaningful difference, weakens the duplicate hypothesis
    strong    – strongly suggests different individuals
    decisive  – forces Different classification (e.g. distinct
                patient IDs from the same study in the narratives)
InconsistencySeverity.title: InconsistencySeverity

IndependenceAssessment.description:
Internal independence assessment produced by the decision logic.

Captures whether the rarity-based matching evidence is strong
enough to reject the null hypothesis that the two reports are
independent draws from the comparison population. A
``NON_INDEPENDENT`` verdict means the matched features are too
unlikely to have arisen by chance under that null; the duplicate
vs otherwise-related distinction is then made by the
``DuplicateRelationship`` sub-label using inconsistency signals.

The user-facing label is derived from this enum (plus
``DuplicateRelationship``) by ``ClassificationResult.final_label``;
downstream consumers should depend on the final label rather than
on this raw enum.

The rarity-zone path assigns only ``NON_INDEPENDENT`` or
``INDEPENDENT``. The shared-source override path additionally
assigns ``NON_INDEPENDENT`` paired with
``DuplicateRelationship.ABSTAIN`` for epistemically underdetermined
same-source scenarios. ``IndependenceAssessment.ABSTAIN`` itself is
kept as a defensive backstop but is not emitted by standard paths.

See: docs/duplicate_adjudication_spec.md § Independence assessment and § Relationship assessment
IndependenceAssessment.title: IndependenceAssessment

IndependenceReason.description:
Audit trail for which branch in the decision logic fired.

Attached to :class:`ClassificationResult` so downstream review can
tell *why* a pair landed on its independence assessment. The
``RARITY_*`` values correspond to the four L_match zones of the
rarity-based branch; ``SHARED_SOURCE`` is set by the shared-source
override path (when a reliable shared source identifier has been
derived from the narratives) and by the multi-patient two-way
rule that handles ``MULTI_PATIENT_CONTEXT_NO_LINK`` pairs with
``L_match > lmatch_limited``. ``ABSTAIN`` is a defensive backstop
for paths not covered by the above; it is not emitted by any
standard code path.

See: docs/duplicate_adjudication_spec.md § Independence assessment and § Relationship assessment
IndependenceReason.title: IndependenceReason

PenaltyTerm.description:
One severity's contribution to ``w_tot``.

Carries the ``weight`` **actually applied** by the run, not the default,
so the arithmetic can be reproduced from the result alone.
PenaltyTerm.title: PenaltyTerm

description:
Full duplicate-adjudication output for a report pair.

Two layered internal labels are produced by the decision logic:

* ``independence_assessment`` — whether the rarity-based matching
  evidence is strong enough to reject the null hypothesis that the
  two reports are independent draws from the comparison population.
* ``duplicate_relationship`` — when independence has been rejected,
  a sub-label that uses inconsistency signals to distinguish a
  likely-duplicate case from one that is linked by something other
  than being the same individual case (e.g. same reporter, same
  study).

Use ``final_label`` for the user-facing label
(``Duplicates`` / ``Otherwise_related`` / ``Unrelated``); downstream
consumers should depend on this rather than on the raw internal
fields. ``penalty`` is the exception: it is diagnostic, carried so that
the inconsistency arithmetic behind the decision can be displayed and
audited without reconstructing it.
title: ClassificationResult
